<solution_file path="src/solution.py">
import pandas as pd

def select_indicators():
    # Load the indicator descriptions
    indicator_descriptions = pd.read_csv('inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv')

    # Load the metadata tables to get themes
    metadata_tables = pd.read_csv('inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv')

    # Merge the two dataframes to get all necessary information
    merged_data = pd.merge(indicator_descriptions, metadata_tables, on='indicator_id', how='left')

    # Filter indicators relevant to urban mobility and livability
    mobility_indicators = merged_data[
        (merged_data['theme'].str.contains('mobility', case=False, na=False)) |
        (merged_data['theme'].str.contains('population_density', case=False, na=False)) |
        (merged_data['theme'].str.contains('environment', case=False, na=False)) |
        (merged_data['theme'].str.contains('living_conditions', case=False, na=False))
    ]

    # Select 10-15 relevant indicators
    selected_indicators = mobility_indicators.head(15)

    # Define justification and expected_direction for each indicator
    selected_indicators['justification'] = selected_indicators.apply(
        lambda row: f"Relevant to {row['theme']} and urban livability.",
        axis=1
    )

    selected_indicators['expected_direction'] = 'contextual'

    # Save the selected indicators to a CSV file
    selected_indicators[['indicator_id', 'indicator_name', 'theme', 'justification', 'expected_direction']].to_csv(
        'outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv', index=False, quoting=1
    )

if __name__ == '__main__':
    select_indicators()
